core_obligations: Set up the index category (proof lines 8040-8066): the author introduces the filtered category of etale neighbourhoods of the geometric point sbar and computes the stalk of R^n f_*F as a colimit of cohomology groups over those neighbourhoods, using the Cech-to-cohomology spectral sequence.

Compare with the strict henselization (proof lines 8066-8094): cohomology over the strict henselization is the colimit of the cohomologies over the etale neighbourhoods, so the two sides agree; the derived statement for K in D^+(X_etale) follows by the same comparison applied to a representative complex.
proof_roadmap: Write the stalk of the higher direct image as a filtered colimit over the etale neighbourhoods of the geometric point.
Identify cohomology over the strict henselization with the colimit of the cohomologies over those neighbourhoods.
Conclude the identification for sheaves, then for bounded below complexes by choosing a representative.
difficulty_reason: The theorem identifies the stalk of a higher direct image along a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism at a geometric point with the cohomology of the base change to the strict henselization, and states the same for bounded below complexes (statement lines 8014-8038). The proof first writes the stalk as a filtered colimit of cohomology groups over the etale neighbourhoods of the geometric point, using the Cech-to-cohomology spectral sequence (proof lines 8040-8066), and then identifies cohomology over the strict henselization with that same colimit, which gives the sheaf case, the derived case following by taking a representative complex (proof lines 8066-8094). The non-formal content is the identification of the two colimits. The claim is H2: two comparisons of colimits, both written out.
